profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company, traded as NVDA and registered with CIK 0001045810, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its most recent 10-K, covering the period ending 2026-01-25, reported revenue of $215,938,000,000.

Per its own site, NVIDIA's AI work centers on the Nemotron family of multimodal, open models, which the company describes as built for long-running, self-evolving agents and for agentic reasoning in graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. The site lists Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for specialized tasks and NeMo Switchyard for routing each step to the right model. Nemotron models are offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices for deployment, and the company says it publishes training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license allowing commercial use and derivatives without crediting NVIDIA. Related tools named on the site include NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Blueprints, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TensorRT-LLM, along with the open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM, and hardware such as NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. Deployment through NIM microservices requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, and models can be tried or downloaded from build.nvidia.com. The site quotes Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, on the vision behind Nemotron, and cites ServiceNow among ecosystem partners.

The litigation record held for NVIDIA shows exposure in California, with 264 cases.
